title: Flip the Vowels
statement:
You get a string s. Reverse the order of its vowels only, and leave every other character where it is. Return the new string.

The vowels are a, e, i, o, u in lower case and upper case. A vowel keeps its case when it moves.

examples.why: The vowels are a, i. Reversed they are i, a, written back into the same two slots.
The vowels u, e, u, e become e, u, e, u. The consonant Q stays first.
Upper-case vowels count too, and they keep their case. The dash is not a letter and does not move.

constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters
hints: The consonants never move. Only the vowels' order changes. Where does the first vowel end up?
The first vowel swaps with the last vowel, the second with the second-to-last, and so on.
Two pointers from both ends of the string. Move each one inward until it sits on a vowel, swap, then step both.

explain.intuition:
Reversing a sequence means swapping the first and last item, then the second and second-to-last, until you meet in the middle. Here the sequence is just the vowels, scattered between other characters.

So run two pointers from both ends of the string. Each pointer skips non-vowels until it lands on a vowel. Then swap the two vowels and move both inward. Strings are immutable in JavaScript and Python, so work on an array of characters and join it at the end.
steps: Convert s into a character array. Set lo = 0, hi = n − 1.
While lo < hi: move lo right while it is not on a vowel, and hi left while it is not on a vowel (both staying below/above the other).
If lo < hi, swap the two characters, then lo++ and hi--.
Join the array and return it.
pitfalls: Checking only lower-case vowels. "Ab-cE" has two vowels, both upper case.
Letting the inner skip loops run past each other, so a vowel gets swapped back out of place or the index goes out of range.
Building the result with string concatenation in a loop, which turns an O(n) idea into O(n²) work in some languages.

solutions.title: Collect vowels, write them back reversed
solutions.idea: Gather the vowels in order, then walk the string again and replace each vowel with the next one from the end of that list.

solutions.title: Two pointers
solutions.idea: Pointers from both ends skip consonants; whenever both sit on vowels, swap them and step inward.

followups: Reverse only the letters of the string and keep every other character in place. What changes in the skip test?
The string is Unicode text with accented vowels like é. What breaks, and how would you define a vowel?
